floor_history.headline: Recon: stale 119 migration pin killed — honest floor is 57/173 (insn-count already exact); residual is one OR-association copy + the count-1 comparand carrier, both pass-attributed from the .loop dump

Floor 57 -> 52 in pure ordinary C: declaring `complement` inside the inner loop spends loop.c's first move (threshold -= 3) so the `count - 1` comparand stays inline, which retires s1's variable-reuse

Floor 52 -> 31 in ordinary C: fold-const's associate: block aims the OR-chain constant (write it next to the OTHER term), a late `i = 0;` fixes the $s1/$s2 pair, and one arm-local `*dst++` swaps the s

Found the missing 173rd instruction: the target inlines dst++ on the COLOUR arm, not the zero-pixel arm — form f1 is 43/173 with a structurally exact inner loop, and its whole residual is a one-atom s

Enumerate modality: 4,488 spellings swept across four regions on three chassis, ZERO hit — the blend block's naming/order/operand space and the outer declaration block's ordering space are both exhaus

Seat question re-framed from the target's own asm: the TARGET compiles with the same weighted reg_n_refs we do (src 32 / dst 26), so the banked 'refs move on pseudo 109' framing is not how the origina

Solver: the residual is FOUR pseudos (src/dst AND j/complement) and the two pairs are independent 1-atom sub-problems; the j/complement half needs j's live_length to merely TIE complement's (52, not 4
Forensics: the cursor seat is a STATEMENT-COUNT question (flow.c:2081, depth-3 weighting) - three pre-RA src++ statements give src refs 26 and the target's $a3/$a2 seat in ordinary C (new chassis q1,

rederive: m2c confirms f1 IS the target's emitted shape, and the ORIGINAL cc1psx seats f1's cursors the same way ours does - the 3-session 'same refs, different seat' contradiction is the C, not the t

Floor 31 -> 29 at the target's own 173 insns: flow_analysis runs BEFORE combine (toplev.c:2983 vs 3004), so two extra depth-3 dst references bought in reg_n_refs and refunded by combine flip the curso

frontier.hypothesis: The banked 29 form's reference lift is spelled as a net-zero increment/decrement pair on a local, which is a FAKE-family construct and is NOT submittable as written; the same +6 lift may have an ORDINARY-C spelling, and if it does the whole cursor result becomes free.
frontier.mechanism: Only +6 weighted refs are needed (two depth-3 occurrences of pseudo 109), not the +12 the round-trip delivers. Any construct that survives to flow_analysis and is then removed or absorbed by combine_instructions qualifier - and combine's own log for this function shows it routinely eats (set p (plus base K)) address computations and HI-load + ashift extension pairs. The sanctioned duplicated-statement-into-arms family (.claude/rules/duplicated-statement-into-arms.md) is the other candidate route, since sinking the shared dst++ into arms adds (N-1) x 6 refs, but it costs emitted instructions unless jump2's cross-jump (minimum 2 matching insns, jump.c:2020) re-merges them.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate ordinary-C statements that put two more depth-3 occurrences of dst into the pre-combine RTL at zero emitted cost - candidates: expressing the inner loop's trip test or the LoadImage argument in terms of dst rather than dst_buf, and an arm-local dst-based address that combine folds into an existing store. Measure each with sandbox and read dst's nrefs from BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG (target: 32-37, keeping livelen 58). If none reaches 32, file a ruling-request asking whether a net-zero increment/decrement pair on a local sits inside the dead-store family (.claude/rules/dead-store-fake-exception.md, whose text describes a same-value re-store / self-assign) - that classification, not the bytes, is what gates this candidate.

frontier.hypothesis: The j/complement pair ($t5/$t4 where the target has $t4/$t5) is the same allocno-order question the cursors just were, and the reg_n_refs / pre-combine framing that solved the cursors should price it directly.
frontier.mechanism: On f1 the census rows are pseudo 116 (nrefs 11, livelen 52, pri 6346) and pseudo 115 (nrefs 11, livelen 57, pri 5789), allocated at ord 15 and 16 into $t4 and $t5. They are adjacent in the order, so a single reference or a five-insn live-length move swaps them - and s7's kill of this pair was measured before the pre-combine framing existed, so it should be re-measured on the new 29 chassis rather than trusted.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/nrefs_census.py --above on the new candidate for the j/complement pair to get the exact lift, then re-measure the s7 forms (tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s7/u1_c_before_j.c .. u4_f) on the 29 chassis. Confirm with BB2_ALLOC_DEBUG that the cursor seat survives each variant before scoring it.

frontier.hypothesis: The blend arm's temp naming and the mflo/srl interleave are a scheduler question, and sched.c's decisions are now known to be the pass that also sets the live lengths feeding allocation - so tools/sched_solver can be pointed at the new 29 chassis directly.
frontier.mechanism: The target runs the blue channel's srl/andi/mult before its first mflo while we run it after; sbs2.py shows this as a 4-insn deletion at target 104-107 against a 4-insn insertion at ours 109-112, with the surrounding temps renamed as a consequence. sched.c:5106 means any reordering here also perturbs live lengths, so the two effects must be read together rather than modelled separately.
frontier.next_probe: Dump the .sched RTL for the new candidate, feed the blend block to tools/sched_solver, and enumerate the source-side orderings of the three channel computations (r, g, b) that put the blue channel's mult ahead of the first mflo. Gate every variant on build_insns == 173 and on the cursor seat still reading dst -> $a2 in ALLOCDBG.
